findings.title: Login IDP cache is not invalidated when updating an IDP belonging to a disabled organization
findings.body:
In `update(IdentityProviderModel model)`, `idpById` is loaded via `getById(model.getInternalId())`, which wraps the model with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`. For an IDP linked to an organization, the wrapper overrides `isEnabled()` to return `org != null && provider.isEnabled() && org.isEnabled() && super.isEnabled()`. However, `getForLogin` populates `IdentityProviderListQuery` from `idpDelegate.getForLogin(...)`, which only checks the IDP's own `enabled` column in the database and ignores whether the organization is currently enabled.

If an organization is disabled (`org.isEnabled() == false`) after the login cache was populated, `getLoginPredicate().test(idpById)` evaluates to `false` even though the IDP's `internalId` is cached in `IdentityProviderListQuery`. If the IDP is then updated while the organization is disabled so that it should no longer be available for login (e.g., setting `hideOnLogin = true`, `linkOnly = true`, `BROKER_PUBLIC = "false"`, or `enabled = false`), `getLoginPredicate().test(updated)` also evaluates to `false`. `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` hits `if (!getLoginPredicate().test(original) && !getLoginPredicate().test(updated)) return;` and skips invalidating `cacheKeyForLogin`. When the organization is subsequently re-enabled, the stale `IdentityProviderListQuery` remains in cache and continues to serve the hidden, link-only, or non-public IDP on the login page. The same issue occurs in reverse when a disabled/hidden org IDP is updated to qualify for login via a wrapped `IdentityProviderModel` while its organization is disabled.

findings.title: InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove skips ID invalidation on alias cache miss and can throw NPE
findings.body:
In `remove(String alias)`, `storedIdp` is now unconditionally fetched via `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` at line 100, but lines 101-109 still branch on `isInvalid(cacheKey)` and whether `cacheKeyIdpAlias` is present in `realmCache`:

1. If an IDP was cached by `internalId` (for example via `getForLogin`, `getByOrganization`, or `getById`) without `getByAlias(alias)` having been called, `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is `false` and `cached` is `null`. `registerIDPInvalidation` is never called even though `storedIdp` was just loaded, leaving `storedIdp.getInternalId()` (and any `IdentityProviderListQuery` entries keyed by `cacheKeyOrgId` that depend on `internalId` invalidation) stale in the cache.
2. If `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is `true` and `remove` is called for an alias that no longer exists (`storedIdp == null`), `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` throws a `NullPointerException` when dereferencing `idp.getInternalId()`.
3. When `cached` is present and valid in `realmCache`, `idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` is still executed unnecessarily instead of reusing `cached.getIdentityProvider()`.

findings.title: getForLogin returns disabled identity providers when their organization is disabled
findings.body: `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` specifies that returned identity providers must be enabled, not link-only, and not hidden on login. In `InfinispanIdentityProviderStorageProvider.getForLogin` (lines 218, 249, and 254), each returned `IdentityProviderModel` is wrapped with `createOrganizationAwareIdentityProviderModel`, whose `isEnabled()` returns `false` when its linked organization (or `OrganizationProvider`) is disabled. However, `getForLogin` does not filter the returned stream by `IdentityProviderModel::isEnabled`. While `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` was updated in this PR to work around this by re-checking `idp.isEnabled()`, any other caller of `getForLogin` will receive disabled identity providers when an organization is disabled.

findings.title: Test cleanup in testCacheIDPForLogin uses literal "alias" instead of the created IDP alias
findings.body: At lines 381 and 425 of `OrganizationCacheTest.testCacheIDPForLogin`, cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` using the literal string `"alias"` instead of `idpRep.getAlias()`. Consequently, cleanup attempts to delete a non-existent IDP named `"alias"` and leaves the realm-level identity providers created by the test (`idp-alias-0` through `idp-alias-9`) in the test realm after the test finishes.
